a.name: Mega 2560 R3 compatible board + data cable
a.spec: ATmega2560, 5 V logic, full-size R3 layout, CH340 USB; e-Gizmo code 210200006, USB cable included
a.why: Runs the preheat, batch timer, basket motion and three flavor selections. Its many input/output pins avoid extra expansion boards; without a controller the automatic sequence cannot run.

a.name: MAX6675 module with bench K-type probe
a.spec: e-Gizmo code 580022730; module accepts 3.3-5 V and is used at 5 V; stock probe for room/warm-water bench tests only
a.why: Converts the very small K-type sensor signal into readable digital temperature data. Reuse the converter in the final machine; the included probe is not assumed suitable for cooking oil.

a.name: Oil-immersion K-type probe with clamp
a.spec: Ungrounded junction, documented food-contact stainless sheath, continuous immersion rating at least 250 C (prefer 300 C), high-temperature lead and K-type extension; exact part awaiting quote
a.store: PH instrumentation supplier / authorized RS or element14 distributor
a.why: Measures actual oil temperature so the controller can show READY and detect faults. Generic threaded or waterproof probes are not automatically food safe or oil rated; the wrong probe can fail or contaminate food.

a.name: IR through-beam emitter/receiver pairs
a.spec: DFRobot SEN0503; 3-5 V supply, use 5 V; NPN normally-open output; 50 cm sensing at 5 V; indoor, not waterproof, max ambient 60 C
a.why: One beam detects potatoes in the cutter chute; the other detects a sachet at the common flavor exit. Breaking a beam gives a clear event; without it the machine cannot confirm loading or packet delivery. Chutes must force all items through the beams.

a.name: 16x2 LCD with I2C backpack
a.spec: HD44780-compatible LCD + PCF8574 backpack, 5 V, Makerlab MLE00659
a.why: Shows oil temperature, PREHEAT, timer, movement and faults. Without visible state the operator cannot tell whether it is safe to load another batch; I2C uses only two signal wires.

a.name: BTS7960 / IBT-2 bidirectional driver boards
a.spec: Circuitrocks AB487; two half-bridges form ONE reversible DC motor driver per board; 12 V motor supply, 5 V logic; advertised 43 A is not a continuous board rating
a.why: One board reverses the basket lift and the other reverses the basket rotation/tilt. Both are tested with small motors then reused if final current tests pass; the controller cannot supply motor current directly.

a.name: Small 12 V geared DC motion simulators
a.spec: N20 or JGA25-family, 12 V, approx. 30-100 rpm, low-current/light-load version; exact variant to verify; never lift a hot basket
a.why: Allows both direction-control channels, end stops and timeouts to be tested cheaply with a dry model. These are bench-only motors, not assumed strong enough for the full basket; without them motion logic remains untested.

a.name: Slow geared DC motors for three flavor coils
a.spec: Candidate SGM-370, 12 V, 6 rpm, continuous rotation; one revolution takes about 10 seconds; obtain rated torque/current and test actual coil before committing to all three
a.why: Rotates each vending spiral when its button is pressed. A standard 180-degree hobby servo cannot directly index repeated full turns. Motor torque must move the loaded coil, and coil pitch must mechanically separate one sachet.

a.name: 5 V logic MOSFET motor driver assemblies
a.spec: One IRLZ44N logic-level MOSFET per channel, gate resistor/pulldown, heatsink if needed, 1N5822 3 A flyback diode; only for coil motors with verified stall below 2 A
a.why: Switches the three coil motors in one direction without loading the Mega pins. The diode absorbs the voltage kick when a motor turns off; without these parts the motors cannot be driven safely and can damage the controller.

a.name: Roller-lever microswitches
a.spec: KW11-3Z-style COM/NO/NC contacts; use as low-voltage signals: lift top/bottom (2), tilt home/dump (2), coil index/home (3), bag-holder engagement (1)
a.why: Reports each motion end position, one coil revolution and a correctly engaged bag holder. Timed motors alone drift or stall; without feedback the basket may overrun or the dispenser may keep turning. These are not safety-rated guard switches.

a.name: Non-illuminated panel pushbuttons
a.spec: Momentary normally-open low-voltage contacts; three flavor selections, one ARM/PREHEAT and one CANCEL/RESET
a.why: Lets the operator deliberately preheat/arm, cancel/reset and select one of three packets. The potato sensor starts the cook timer automatically once READY; flavor selection requires button release before another vend.

a.name: Latching mushroom emergency stop
a.spec: Documented positive-opening NC contacts, preferably 2 NC + auxiliary feedback; IEC 60947-5-5 compliant component; exact supplier part to quote
a.why: Requests immediate removal of heater and motor power through the separate hardware safety circuit, even if software hangs. A button connected only to a GPIO cannot reliably stop a failed controller. Reused in the final panel.

a.name: Buzzer and status LED kit
a.spec: 5 V active buzzer driven through 2N2222/BC337 with base resistor; red/green LEDs with individual 330-ohm resistors
a.why: Sounds a fault/end-of-cycle alarm and shows ready/fault status. A transistor supplies buzzer current rather than burdening a controller pin; LEDs need resistors to avoid excessive current.

a.name: 830-point solderless breadboards
a.spec: MB102-style, signal and low-current logic circuits only
a.why: Holds the logic connections for reversible experimentation without soldering. Motor power, contactor wiring and mains must use terminals instead; putting them through breadboard contacts can overheat the contacts.

a.name: 40-pin jumper wire bundles
a.spec: One bundle each male-male, male-female and female-female, approx. 20 cm; select matching variants
a.status: LISTED FROM; variant price may differ
a.why: Connects controller signals, sensor outputs and display during testing. Different end types match board sockets and module pins; without them the bench circuit cannot be interconnected.

a.name: Enclosed 12 V regulated wall adapter
a.spec: 12 V DC, 3 A, locally compliant enclosed adapter, matching center-positive connector; only small motors, one at a time
a.why: Supplies the low-voltage dry prototype without exposed mains terminals. It is not the final basket-motor supply; inadequate current causes resets or failed motor starts.

a.name: 12 V to 5 V buck converter
a.spec: LM2596S adjustable module, configured to 5.0 V before connecting; budget less than 1 A for logic, not motors or servos
a.why: Reduces 12 V to the 5 V needed by logic, display and sensors. Motors stay on 12 V; feeding 12 V to 5 V parts destroys them. Do not trust a cheap module's advertised 3 A as a continuous thermal rating.

a.name: Bench fuse and terminal kit
a.spec: DC-rated fuse holders and spare fuses, covered low-voltage terminals, reverse-polarity protection; initial branch ratings chosen after motor data
a.why: Allows a short or wiring mistake to disconnect a branch before wires overheat. Motors connect through these terminals, not Dupont jumpers; this small bench kit remains workshop equipment.

a.name: Passive components and filtering kit
a.spec: 10 kOhm pulldowns/pullups, 100-ohm gate resistors, 100 nF decoupling/motor caps, 470-1000 uF 25 V motor bulk caps and 470 uF 10 V logic bulk cap; RC input filtering parts
a.why: Keeps driver inputs off during boot and absorbs motor noise/current pulses. Without filtering and a sound ground layout the timer or sensor inputs can glitch and the controller can restart.

a.name: DC motor branch current sensor modules
a.spec: ACS712-20A, 5 V supply and analog output, one for lift and one for tilt; genuine chip, properly rated board terminals; DC use only
a.why: Detects a blocked basket through excessive current and helps measure power demand. Software thresholds need calibration; these sensors supplement fuses and timeouts and do not independently make motion safe.

b.name: Complete electric deep fryer with basket
b.spec: Price candidate Hanabishi HFRY60SS: 6 L, 230 V, 2400 W, variable thermostat; REQUIRE documented independent overheat cutoff and grounding before acceptance; exact accepted protected model pending
b.why: Provides a manufactured oil tank, heater, thermostat and basket instead of an improvised exposed heater. Its thermostat regulates heat throughout preheat/cooking. Included once at your request; it may be purchased by the mechanical team instead.

b.name: Load-rated basket lift and rotation motors
b.spec: Two 12 V reversible geared actuators; output torque, speed, gearbox duty and brake requirements calculated from actual basket/linkage; prefer worm/braked mechanism; exact models NOT selected
b.store: PH industrial motor supplier / verified Shopee or Lazada seller
b.why: Moves the real basket up to drain and rotates it to the receiving chute. They replace the two small bench simulators. Fry weight alone cannot establish torque; undersized motors stall and unrestrained baskets can fall when power is cut.

b.name: Genuine 12 V industrial power supply
b.spec: Candidate MEAN WELL LRS-150-12: 12 V, 12.5 A, 150 W; 230 V selector setting and installation by electrician; final selection depends on startup/stall measurements
b.store: Authorized MEAN WELL PH supplier / RS PH / element14 PH
b.why: Powers the full-size actuators and 5 V buck converter. The 3 A bench adapter cannot be assumed adequate. Genuine supply ratings and a motor-current margin avoid brownouts; terminals must be enclosed and earthed.

b.name: Enclosed heater and motion power-control assembly
b.spec: Electrician-designed enclosure: suitably rated heater run contactor plus independent safety disconnect, low-voltage isolated control supply/interface, hardware E-stop/guard chain, manual restart, fuse/RCBO protection, protective-earth bus, mains cables/glands and covered terminals; no claim of certified safety performance
b.store: Licensed PH electrician / industrial panel supplier
b.why: Lets logic grant heater permission while the fryer's own thermostat controls temperature. A separate hardwired stop removes heater and motor power, not just a GPIO signal. Includes mains power enclosure/wiring but excludes reused E-stop, B5 guard and B11 labor.

b.name: Safety guard interlock switch
b.spec: Documented positive-opening guard interlock, low-voltage safety circuit, exact component selected for the actual fixed/movable guard; budget one guarded access point
b.why: Stops dangerous movement and heating when the guarded hot-oil/moving mechanism is exposed. Ordinary KW11 position switches are not a substitute; if the guard has multiple doors, additional interlocks are needed.

b.name: Perfboard or Mega terminal carrier
b.spec: FR4 solder board/terminal carrier, socket headers and covered low-voltage terminals; motors use driver-board high-current terminals separately
b.why: Replaces loose breadboard signal connections with secure soldered or screw-terminal connections that resist vibration. The Mega remains removable for maintenance; no mains is routed on this board.

b.name: Separated electronics enclosure
b.spec: Approx. 250 x 200 x 100 mm flame-retardant box, mounting plate, standoffs and cable glands; size verified from component placement; separate from B4 mains box
b.why: Keeps oil, steam and fingers away from logic and drivers while maintaining required cooling. A sealed box alone does not solve driver heat; without protected mounting the electronics are exposed to shorts and grease.

b.name: Permanent DC wire, connectors and branch fuses
b.spec: Flexible stranded wire and locking connectors with documented current ratings, ferrules, separate motor/logic branch fuse holders; 16-18 AWG motor wire only if calculations permit; sensor wiring separate
b.why: Carries motor current and makes parts removable without loose breadboard contacts. Connector and fuse ratings must match the actual load; a generic JST or KF301 label is not proof of suitability for high current.

b.name: Flex cable and strain-relief set
b.spec: Heat/grease-resistant flexible sensor cable, high-flex loop at moving basket, clamps, protective sleeving and cable glands; motion carrier supplied by mechanical team
b.why: Prevents movement from pulling a temperature wire or exposing conductors. Ordinary rigid leads fatigue when repeatedly bent; a disconnected or snagged sensor can interrupt the cycle or misreport temperature.

b.name: Panel hardware and identification kit
b.spec: Screws/standoffs, labels, heatshrink for low-voltage joints, sensor mounting hardware and drain/splash routing; food-contact brackets supplied by mechanical team
b.why: Holds sensors in alignment and identifies power and stop controls. Poor alignment causes missed strips or sachets; unlabeled wiring makes maintenance and fault diagnosis harder.

b.name: Electrical assembly and commissioning labor
b.spec: Licensed electrician: mains assembly, earthing/protection checks, heater cutoff verification, guarded power-off/restart checks and installation review; service allowance, not a material
b.store: Local licensed electrician / school's qualified electrical supervisor
b.why: The project involves approximately 10-11 A mains heater current and hot oil. Qualified inspection is necessary before live tests; the enclosure and components alone do not prove the assembled machine is safe.

holds: Basket mass (empty basket + mounting + 0.300 kg fries + retained oil), sprocket pitch radius, tilt pivot distance, lift travel and desired speeds are still required. Motor family names alone cannot establish torque.

The drawing does not show a demonstrated trajectory from the raised basket to the right funnel. Mechanical team must supply a linkage/slide/chute solution. Two basket axes are budgeted; an extra transfer axis is excluded until needed.

Select coil motors/driver diodes from loaded-coil torque and stall current. The PHP 500 SGM-370 is a price candidate, not a verified final torque selection. Mechanical pitch/index geometry must release exactly one sachet.

Accept a fryer only after verifying its actual manual/nameplate, independent overheat protection, grounding, minimum/maximum oil level and compatibility with the moving basket. HFRY60SS is a priced candidate on HOLD.

Final power supply, motor driver capability, fuses and conductor sizes need actual startup/stall current. The hardware stop must remove heater/motor energy and require deliberate restart; a brake or mechanical load restraint must prevent basket free-fall.
operation: ARM starts thermostat-controlled preheating. READY requires the validated oil temperature, basket home, fitted bag holder and closed guards. The drop sensor starts loading/cycle detection; it does not turn off temperature regulation or guarantee a full batch.

The first valid potato drop while READY starts the requested configurable 600-second timer automatically. Subsequent strips from the same manual cut do not restart it or create another batch. A short loading window must be validated for the cutter; later loading during cooking is prohibited.

At timer completion: remove heater permission, lift with top-stop/current/timeout checks, drain above the tank, confirm bag/guard, then rotate along the mechanically validated path and dump through the right funnel. Return tilt home before lowering.

One flavor press runs only that coil through one indexed revolution. Confirm a packet at the common exit, stop on timeout/no delivery and require button release before another vend. Two detected packets flag a fault; sensor feedback cannot undo a double feed.

Ten minutes is the user's requested setting, not a universal fry standard. Validate time and oil temperature with the actual cut size and 300 g batch before food use. Never heat an empty tank or add wet potatoes/water to hot oil.

Phase 2 begins only after explicit BOM approval. Dry prototype first, no mains on breadboards. Oil/mains commissioning requires the protected fryer, independent stop/protection assembly, mechanical guarding and qualified inspection.
